The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to launch a **Google Cloud** virtual machine that has an **RTX‑A6000 style GPU** (or the closest equivalent that’s actually available at the moment) and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick start – `gcloud` CLI  

```bash
PROJECT_ID="my-project-id"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
ZONENAME="us-central1-b"

# NOTE:
#   • As of now, GCP does NOT offer an “NVIDIA RTX A6000” SKU.
#     The nearest high‑end option is the *Tesla A100* (PCIe).
#
#   • Replace `--accelerator=...` below with whatever GPU you really need
#     once your target hardware becomes available.

gcloud beta compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONENAME" \
  --machine-type=e2-highcpu-16 \          # 16 vCPU / 64 GB RAM
  --boot-disk-size=120GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # see section 2
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100-pcie-40gb \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE
```

### What each flag means  
| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type=` | CPU/RAM size (`e2`, `n1`, `c2d`, …). Pick one that fits your workload. |
| `--accelerator=` | Adds a GPU. Use `count=N` & `type=[GPU_TYPE]`. Currently supported types include `nvidia-tesla-k80`, `p4`, `t4`, `v100`, `a100-*`, etc. |
| `--image-family=/project=` | Installs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS automatically. |
| `startup-script=` | Optional shell script that installs CUDA/NVIDIA driver after boot. |

#### Example `startup.sh`
```bash
#!/bin/bash
apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y
apt-get install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004_11.7.0-1_amd64.deb
dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004_11.7.0-1_amd64.deb
apt-key adv --fetch-keys http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/7fa2af80.pub
apt-get update
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
echo '/usr/local/nvidia/lib:/usr/local/nvidia/lib64' >> ~/.profile
```

Run `chmod +x startup.sh` before executing the `gcloud` command above.

---

## 2️⃣ Full REST‑API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to hit the Compute Engine REST endpoint directly (for automation scripts, Terraform providers, etc.), here’s a minimal payload you’d POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<YOUR_PROJECT>/zones/<YOUR_ZONE>/instances
Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `<YOUR_PROJECT>` and `<YOUR_ZONE>` appropriately.

### Sample Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "<INSTANCE_NAME>",
  "description": "VM with high‑performance GPU",
  "labels": {
      "env":"demo",
      "purpose":"testing"
  },
  "machineType": "projects/<YOUR_PROJECT>/zones/<YOUR_ZONE>/machineTypes/e2-highcpu-16",

  "disks": [
    {
      "deviceName": "bootdisk",
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 120,
        "diskType": "pd-balanced"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "boot": true,
      "mode": "READ_WRITE"
    }
  ],

  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}],
      "subnetworks": ["global/networks/default"]
    }
  ],

  "serviceAccounts": [{
    "email": "default@<YOUR_PROJECT>.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
    "scopes": [ "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/devstorage.read_write",
                "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/logging.write",
                "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/monitoring.write",
                "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/servicecontrol",
                "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/service.management.readonly",
                "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email",
                "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" ]
  }],

  "guestAccelerators": [
    { 
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<YOUR_PROJECT>/locations/<YOUR_ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100-pcie-40gb"
    }
  ],

  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },

  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y curl gnupg ca-certificates\ndpkg -i $(curl -fsSL https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004_11.7.0-1_amd64.deb)\napt-key adv --fetch-keys http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/7fa2af80.pub\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-drivers\n"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> ⚠️ **Important:**  
> *GCP doesn’t ship an official “RTX A6000” GPU.*  
> You’ll either need to wait until Google adds that specific SKU or choose another high‑end GPU (like the Tesla A100 PCIe). Adjust `"acceleratorType"` accordingly.

---

## 3️⃣ Verify Instance Creation

After launching, confirm everything worked:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe $INSTANCE_NAME --zone=$ZONENAME
```

Look under the `status` field → it should read `RUNNING`.

Check attached GPU:

```bash
ssh $INSTANCE_NAME -- zone=$ZONENAME <<EOF
lspci | grep -E 'VGA|Display'
EOF
```

Or inside the VM run:

```bash
sudo lshw -C display
```

Both commands should list the NVIDIA GPU along with its memory capacity (~48 GiB for an RTX A6000).

---

## TL;DR

| Tool | Command / Payload |
|------|-------------------|
| **CLI** | `gcloud beta compute instances create INSTANCE_NAME --accelerator count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100-pcie-40gb ...` |
| **REST** | POST to `/projects/PID/zones/ZD/instances` with JSON body shown above |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, accelerator count, or add more disks depending on your exact requirements!
